newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris wants Zaire envoy's immunity lifted.
newsitem.headline: Paris wants Zaire envoy's immunity lifted.

text.p: France asked Zaire on Monday to lift the diplomatic immunity of Zaire's ambassador to Paris after his car killed two French schoolboys on a pedestrian crossing in an accident last month.

"We are asking Zaire to lift the immunity of its ambassador (Ramazani Baya) so that he may present himself to French justice as he has himself suggested," French Foreign Ministry spokesman Yves Doutriaux told reporters.
"It's up to the Zairean authorities to make a decision about lifting his immunity," Doutriaux said.
The accident has caused anger in France about the immunity from prosecution granted to diplomats suspected of crimes. The newspaper France-Soir dubbed Baya the "crusher-ambassador".
Zaire recalled Baya at Paris's request on Sunday after the car he was driving hit the two youths in the Riviera resort of Menton on November 23 while they were on a pedestrian crossing.

Police say he was driving at 100 km an hour (62 mph) in a 45 kph (30 mph) zone. The families of the two schoolboys want Baya, who wrote a letter to the families to express remorse, put on trial over the killings.
An official at the Zairean embassy in Paris said on Monday that Baya had not yet left France. "He's going to leave. He's still in France," the official said.
One of the boys, Raphael Lenoir, 13, died instantly. The other, 12-year-old Ronald Lehartel, died on Saturday. He had been in a coma in hospital since the accident.

Baya was driving through Menton on his way to visit Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko, convalescing at a luxury mansion in nearby Roquebrune Cap Martin. Mobutu underwent cancer surgery in Switzerland in August.

French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette pledged in a letter to the mayor of Menton to work on on the parents' behalf. "They can count on me," he wrote, adding that he would study possible reform of diplomatic immunity.
De Charette also sent letters to the two families.
On Saturday, 4,000 people marched through Menton -- about a sixth of the town's population -- in a silent but angry tribute hours before Ronald Lehartel's death.
Mourners carried white carnations and laid a wreath at the seafront pedestrian crossing where the accident took place.
Asking a country to recall a diplomat is a frequent sanction for envoys suspected of crimes. If Baya leaves, he will be out of reach of any French court unless he chooses to return.
Patrick Lenoir, father of Raphael, has rejected an offer of talks with de Charette.
"This is an attempt to find a compromise," he told the newspaper Le Monde. "Accepting this type of compromise would be to kill my son a second time."
The accident has embarrassed France by putting the focus on Mobutu's presence in a palatial Riviera mansion during a crisis over hundreds of thousands of refugees in eastern Zaire.
France had declared him an unwelcome guest in recent years. He flew to the Riviera almost a month ago after cancer surgery in Switzerland.
Swiss authorities later denied him a visa to return for medical treatment.
